claims.text: What the image looks like RUQ (Morison's pouch): most sensitive view for hemoperitoneum in a supine patient. Anechoic stripe between liver & kidney = free fluid
claims.quote: Most sensitive view for hemoperitoneum in supine patient. Anechoic stripe between liver & kidney = free fluid.

claims.text: LUQ: free fluid often appears between spleen and diaphragm (subphrenic) first - look there before the splenorenal interface
claims.quote: Free fluid often appears between spleen and diaphragm (subphrenic) first - look there before splenorenal interface.

claims.text: Suprapubic: free fluid in the pouch of Douglas (rectouterine, F) or rectovesical pouch (M)
claims.quote: Free fluid in pouch of Douglas (rectouterine, F) or rectovesical pouch (M).

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Probe: curvilinear or phased-array for the four standard FAST views
claims.quote: Probe: curvilinear or phased-array for the four standard FAST views;

claims.text: Sequence (typical): pericardial (subxiphoid) → RUQ (Morison's pouch) → LUQ (perisplenic) → suprapubic
claims.quote: Sequence (typical): 1. Pericardial (subxiphoid) → 2. RUQ (Morison's pouch) → 3. LUQ (perisplenic) → 4. Suprapubic.
claims.locator: FAST & eFAST Exam, Indications, Probe, Sequence, Performance

claims.text: Performance: sensitivity ~80% / specificity > 90% for hemoperitoneum; minimum detectable free fluid ~200-250 mL; Trendelenburg may improve sensitivity in the RUQ
claims.quote: Performance: sensitivity ~80% / specificity >90% for hemoperitoneum; minimum detectable free fluid ~200-250 mL. Trendelenburg may improve sensitivity in RUQ.
claims.locator: FAST & eFAST Exam, Indications, Probe, Sequence, Performance

claims.text: RUQ pearls: sweep through the entire interface; small fluid pockets are often at the hepatic tip or caudal to the liver. Perinephric fat may mimic free fluid (it is hypoechoic but follows the kidney contour)
claims.quote: Sweep through entire interface; small fluid pockets often at hepatic tip or caudal to liver. Perinephric fat may mimic free fluid (perirenal fat is hypoechoic but follows kidney contour).

claims.text: Suprapubic pearls: empty bladder = poor view (consider clamping a Foley); small amounts of pelvic free fluid are normal (physiologic) in reproductive-age females; bowel gas can mimic or obscure
claims.quote: Empty bladder = poor view; consider clamping Foley if needed. Pelvic free fluid is normal in small amounts in reproductive-age females (physiologic). Bowel gas can mimic or obscure.

claims.text: FAST images the pericardium, right and left upper quadrants and pelvis, mainly to find abnormal pericardial fluid or intraperitoneal free fluid; it is sensitive for larger amounts of abdominal fluid but does not identify specific solid organ injuries well, is poor at detecting viscus perforation, and is limited in obesity and with subcutaneous air
claims.quote: The FAST images the pericardium, right and left upper quadrants, and pelvis; its primary aim is to find abnormal pericardial fluid or intraperitoneal free fluid. An extended FAST (E-FAST) adds images of the chest aimed at detecting pneumothorax. Ultrasound gives no radiation exposure and is sensitive for detecting larger amounts of abdominal fluid but does not identify specific solid organ injuries well, is poor at detecting viscus perforation, and is limited in patients with obesity and in patients with subcutaneous air (eg, due to pneumothorax).

claims.text: Causes Blunt trauma (eg, a direct blow, impact with an object or sudden deceleration): the spleen is damaged most commonly, followed by the liver and a hollow viscus (typically the small intestine)
claims.quote: Blunt trauma may involve a direct blow (eg, kick), impact with an object (eg, fall on bicycle handlebars), or sudden deceleration (eg, fall from a height, vehicle crash). The spleen is the organ damaged most commonly, followed by the liver and a hollow viscus (typically the small intestine) (1).

claims.text: Symptoms Abdominal pain is typical but often mild and easily obscured by more painful injuries or altered sensorium; pain from splenic injury sometimes radiates to the left shoulder
claims.quote: Abdominal pain typically is present; however, pain is often mild and thus easily obscured by other, more painful injuries (eg, fractures) and by altered sensorium (eg, due to head injury, intoxication, shock). Pain from splenic injury sometimes radiates to the left shoulder.

claims.text: Vital signs may show hypovolemia (eg, tachycardia, narrow pulse pressure) or shock (eg, dusky skin, diaphoresis, altered sensorium, oliguria, hypotension)
claims.quote: On examination, vital signs may show evidence of hypovolemia (eg, tachycardia, narrow pulse pressure) or shock (eg, dusky skin color, diaphoresis, altered sensorium, oliguria, hypotension).

claims.text: Abdominal distention after trauma typically indicates severe hemorrhage (2 to 3 L), but distention may not be apparent even after loss of several units of blood
claims.quote: Abdominal distention after trauma typically indicates severe hemorrhage (2 to 3 L), but distention may not be apparent even in patients who have lost several units of blood.

claims.text: Peritoneal signs (eg, guarding, rebound), although not very sensitive, strongly suggest intraperitoneal blood and/or intestinal contents
claims.quote: Although not very sensitive, when detected, peritoneal signs (eg, guarding, rebound) strongly suggest the presence of intraperitoneal blood and/or intestinal contents.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: indications: blunt abdominal trauma (especially hypotensive); rapid bedside triage when CT is not feasible; helps decide OR vs CT in unstable patients; less reliable for penetrating trauma
claims.quote: Indications: blunt abdominal trauma (especially hypotensive); rapid bedside triage when CT not feasible. Helps decide OR vs CT in unstable patients. Less reliable for penetrating trauma.
claims.locator: FAST & eFAST Exam, Indications, Probe, Sequence, Performance

claims.text: Her chart: a negative FAST does NOT rule out injury. In stable patients with a concerning mechanism / exam, get CT. Serial FAST may detect evolving hemorrhage
claims.quote: Key limitation: a negative FAST does NOT rule out injury. In stable patients with concerning mechanism / exam, get CT. Serial FAST may detect evolving hemorrhage.
claims.locator: FAST & eFAST Exam, Indications, Probe, Sequence, Performance

claims.text: Some clinicians do a FAST during resuscitation and proceed to laparotomy if a large amount of free fluid is seen (in hypotensive patients); if FAST is negative or weakly positive, CT if there is still concern once the patient is stabilized
claims.quote: Some clinicians perform a FAST scan during the resuscitation phase and proceed to laparotomy if a large amount of free fluid is seen (in hypotensive patients). If FAST results are negative or weakly positive, clinicians perform CT if there is still concern about the abdomen after the patient is stabilized.

claims.text: Hemodynamically unstable patients with abdominal injuries need immediate intervention (eg, laparotomy and/or angiographic embolization), not delayed by CT or other studies
claims.quote: Hemodynamically unstable patients with abdominal injuries require immediate intervention (eg, laparotomy and/or angiographic embolization), which should not be delayed by CT or other diagnostic studies.

claims.text: Unless the patient is unstable and/or requires immediate laparotomy, CT is the preferred imaging modality
claims.quote: Unless the patient is unstable and/or requires immediate laparotomy, CT scan is preferred imaging modality.
